findings.title: The three zone rules' comments name the wrong tests (R3907, R3910, R3913 for what R3906, R3907 and R3908 hold)
findings.what_happens: Straw Poll's rule cites R3907 (Logic Dive's judgement), Logic Dive's cites R3910 (a removed number, 'the trial modes' census as the E73 line numbered it'), Scrum's turn seconds cite R3913 (E99's console schema). The registry's rows for the three rules are R3906, R3907 and R3908 (tests-tier1.mjs:10061, :10084, :10109). The numbers were already so in E73's own commit (git show 5101742c: lines 60, 73, 88).
findings.evidence: * THE STRAW POLL'S RULE (TR3 = 2, the plan's 2/3; R3907) ... * LOGIC DIVE'S JUDGEMENT (TR3 = 2, TR27: simple majority; a tie, 0:0 too, is wrong; R3910) ... * A Scrum turn's seconds (`scrumTurnSeconds`; R3913)
findings.failure_scenario: A developer changing the two-thirds rule follows the comment to R3907, edits the Logic Dive test, and the Straw Poll's real guard R3906 fails unexpectedly - or a rule is believed unguarded because R3910 is removed.
findings.expected: Each comment names the row that holds its rule.
findings.refutation_tried: Read the three rows' titles in the registry and the tests' bodies (R3906 calls strawVerdict, R3907 diveVerdict, R3908 scrumTurnSeconds); R3913's title is the console's schema. Not a renumbering of the registry after the comment: the comment's numbers stand in 5101742c, where R3906-R3908 already held these rules by their titles.

findings.title: A wrong Logic Dive answer shows the right one by elimination: the public card says the class is wrong and gives the counts on a two-answer question
findings.where: scripts/zone-machine.mjs:208-210 (diveJudge's wrong card with words a and b); lang/en.json DRPG.Zones.dive.wrong; scripts/zone-machine.mjs:223-226 (a question has exactly answers a and b)
findings.what_happens: On a wrong majority the card posted to the whole table is 'The class is wrong, with {a} in Zone A and {b} in Zone B. The Logic Dive ends here.' With one answer per zone and the majority's zone named by the counts, every player reads that the other zone's answer is the right one. The notes and e73/STATUS.md (63-64) say a wrong answer, like a tie, 'shows no truth' and the set 'stays replayable'.
findings.evidence: if (verdict !== "right") { return over([card(floor.mode, verdict === "tie" ? "DRPG.Zones.dive.tie" : "DRPG.Zones.dive.wrong", words, { sfx: "answerWrong" })], ...
findings.failure_scenario: The class stands 4:1 in Zone A on question two and is wrong; the card tells everyone the answer is Zone B's; when the GM replays the set later the class answers question two right from memory, which the replay warning ('Players may remember it') only half covers.
findings.expected: The notes and the handbook say that a wrong answer tells the class the other answer, or the default (Q-E73 'a wrong majority shows no truth, as a tie does', owner to confirm) is put to the owner with this reading.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a third answer or a question with more than two (diveQuestion requires a and b and no other); for a whisper of the card (the e71 text batch B17 items 108-109 record it as posted to the whole table); for a test that reads a wrong card (R3904 drives a tie only). It stands as a wording of the promise rather than a code defect: telling the class it was wrong cannot avoid it, so the severity is nit and the question goes to the owner.

l1.what: The zone modes on a real v14 hall (LIVE-E73-01, -02, -05 first; then -03, -04, -06, -07)
recipe: In the sandbox, link a trial hall with two zone regions, one with a hole and one on a second Level; pick them in Room Setup > Scenes.
Start a Straw Poll from the console's mode picker; a player drags a token from Zone A to Zone B in the last two seconds; compare every client's count with the GM's.
Put a token in the hole and one on the second Level; note which side each counts on.
Run a Logic Dive; the primary GM reloads mid-question; note the clock after the reload and search game.settings for the set's truth on a player.
Screenshot the console at 1366x768 with no trial and in a Straw Poll, both themes: footer and bar in view with Foundry's header.
l1.clients: GM, a second GM for the reload, three players
l1.settles_if: Counts agree on every client, the hole on neither side, the Level per testPoint, the question surviving the reload with no truth on a player and the console whole on screen: E73 holds at a table; any count that differs or a truth on a player is a defect against E73.

findings.title: 'Once a trial' is checked on each GM before its write: two GMs pressing Send at once both post the summary
findings.where: scripts/case-summary.mjs:78 (the first check), :92-96 (the second check, then setTrialProgress and ChatMessage.create); scripts/trial-progress.mjs:494-497 (a non-primary GM's patch asked of the primary, with no test of summaryShown there)
findings.what_happens: Each GM's browser reads trialProgress().summaryShown, waits on the preview, reads it again after Send, then asks the record's patch and creates the card itself. The primary applies the patch in its queue but does not refuse a second one, and ChatMessage.create is not behind it; between one GM's Send and the record's update reaching the other GM's browser, the second check passes there as well.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs both have Show summary open after a verdict and press Send within about a second; every player gets two case summary cards and two boards.
findings.expected: The once-a-trial rule held where the record is written (the primary's step refusing a second summaryShown), as the verdict's own lock is.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a lock on the primary: recordPatchOf only filters fields (trial-progress.mjs:518-522); serialWrite orders writes on one browser, not across GMs; scenario 63 S presses gm3's Send after gm2's has landed (sequential). Rare (two GMs, the same second), so nit; LIVE-E99-04's table would show it with two GMs.

findings.title: The schema's Presented marks and hints read the whole chapter's Present cards, so a second trial in the chapter starts with the first trial's
findings.where: scripts/case-hints.mjs:51-66 (casePresentations filters by the chapter flag and withdrawn only); scripts/case-trial.mjs:65
findings.what_happens: Since E99 next the ticks are one trial's (a row stamped with the trial's trialStartedAt), but the presentations the hints rest on are every Present card of the chapter in the chat. In a second Class Trial of the same chapter the GM's schema opens with Remnants marked Presented and deductions hinted from the first trial.
findings.failure_scenario: A chapter's first trial ends on a wrong verdict and a second is opened; before anyone presents, the GM's schema already marks three Remnants Presented and hints a deduction.
findings.expected: Presentations read from the current trial (cards after its entry), as the ticks are.
